---
title: "State-of-Health BC"
---

**State-of-Health BC (SoHBC)** is a project that attempts to describe and
predict the state of health in British Columbia, Canada — from defining
what "health" means here, through the data and causal structures behind
it, to actions that would improve it.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Disclaimer — caveat emptor

State-of-Health BC is an **independent project**. It is not officially
endorsed by, affiliated with, or produced by any organisation — including
the Government of British Columbia, the Provincial Health Services
Authority (PHSA), the BC Centre for Disease Control (BCCDC), any regional
health authority, the First Nations Health Authority, or any other body.
It does not speak for them, and any errors are the project's own. This
remains the case until further notice.
:::

The project is early stage. This site is the project's documentation and
will grow alongside the analysis.

Two principles frame everything here. Health is treated as **dynamic and
nonstationary** — a trajectory that changes over time, along with the
relationships behind it ([why](explanation/nonstationarity.qmd)). And
while the object of study is BC's health, the data explaining it are
not limited to BC-origin data ([why](explanation/why-bc.qmd)).

## The journey

1. Defining health, and the state of health in BC.
2. Finding and exploring data that describe the state of health in BC
   over time and space — "data" construed broadly, from microdata to
   published summary statistics.
3. Characterising the variables that are statistically dependent with
   health.
4. Characterising the causal structures that result in changes in the
   state of health.
5. Recommending actions that would improve the **cumulative** state of
   health over time (maximising the time-integrated state of health across
   individuals and cohorts).
